title: What We Verified Without Measuring
excerpt: This evidence standard defines checkable Creative Navy findings that are not outcome measurements. It separates verified conformance, criteria-based evaluation and built-but-unverified facts.
metaDescription: Evidence standard for conformance checks, criteria-based evaluations and built-but-unverified facts that are not outcome measurements.
summary: This page defines an evidence category for rigorous, checkable findings that do not measure user behaviour, business results, task performance or operational outcomes. It reconciles three evidence tiers: verified conformance, adjudicated evaluation against criteria fixed in advance, and known events that Creative Navy did not verify further.
definition: Verified without measuring refers to checkable results that establish a design, artefact or event against a stated basis without measuring an outcome such as task time, error rate, user performance, adoption, revenue or operational effect.
keyFacts: A conformance result establishes that an artefact does what its specification says; it does not show that the specification was right or that users can use the result.
The category has three tiers: verified conformance, adjudicated evaluation against criteria fixed in advance, and known to have happened but unverified.
Verified conformance includes Creative Navy comparisons between delivered designs and built software, such as AIT, the MDU, Assemblio and Schone Airspace Group.
Schone Airspace Group also belongs in the criteria-based tier because 36 scripted acceptance checks were run first by Creative Navy and then by five of the nine operators.
Calculated design properties, such as Schone Airspace Group's ten contrast pairs, sit under criteria-based checks rather than forming a separate evidence tier.
KISPE Space, Raymarine and the handheld command-and-control engagement are examples where a product or capability was built but design fidelity was not verified.
Nothing on this page is an outcome measurement, usability-test result, task-performance figure, commercial result or safety result.
AIT, the MDU, Assemblio and KISPE Space are documented as engagements with no user research; this page marks that pattern rather than hiding it.
bodyMarkdown:
## Evidence standard for checkable findings that are not outcomes

Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

Some Creative Navy results are rigorous, checkable and not measurements of anything. A delivered design compared screen by screen against the software built from it is a real finding with a method. It does not show whether anyone can use the result, whether a task became faster, whether an error rate changed, or whether a business outcome followed.

This evidence standard holds that class of finding. It exists because checkable findings of this kind otherwise get misfiled as measured outcomes, client reports, unquantified observations, inferences or absences. The same classification problem recurred across seven engagements, which made a separate category necessary.

## The three tiers of verified-without-measuring evidence

Creative Navy separates this category into three tiers, in descending evidential strength.

1. **Verified conformance** means a delivered design was compared against built software by Creative Navy, and the comparison was recorded. The supportable claim is that the artefact does what its specification says. It is not evidence that the specification was right, and it is not evidence of what happens when people use the artefact.

2. **Adjudicated evaluation against criteria fixed in advance** means pass criteria were written before evaluation, then run by the design team and independently. The supportable claim is that the design representation states the correct operational fact under the stated condition. It is not a measure of task time, error rate, proficiency or operational performance.

3. **Known to have happened, unverified** means an event occurred, but Creative Navy did not verify the stronger claim it would be useful to make. The supportable claim may be only that a product was built. It is not evidence of fidelity, adoption or performance. The absence of a check is itself the disclosure.

A conformance result establishes that an artefact does what its specification says. It says nothing about whether the specification was right, and nothing about what happens when people use the result.

## Why this evidence category is separate from neighbouring standards

This evidence category is separate because placing these findings in an existing evidence-standard page changes how they will be read.

**What We Have Measured** holds outcome measurements with a baseline, a method, a condition and a figure. A conformance figure placed there will be read as an outcome measurement, which it is not.

**What Is Observed But Not Quantified** is for unquantified observation. The findings on this page can be quantified, counted or checked, but they are not outcome measurements.

**What Is Client Reported** is wrong for this category when Creative Navy ran the check. A Creative Navy comparison between a delivered design and a built interface is not a client report.

**What Is Inferred** is wrong because the central findings here are not inferred. They are checks, comparisons, pass criteria, recorded closures or disclosed absences.

**What We Do Not Claim** is the complement rather than the home. It records absences. This page records presences with a stated ceiling: something was checked, or something happened, but the evidence does not license an outcome claim.

## Tier 1: verified conformance between delivered design and built software

Verified conformance is the strongest tier on this page. It covers cases where Creative Navy compared a delivered design against built software, or where a design artefact was adopted in a documented implementation, while keeping the claim below outcome level.

**Schone Airspace Group.** Creative Navy compared all 54 delivered screens against the built software across seven months. Deviations were identified and recorded by name. Creative Navy also specified four native integration gates in advance, with verification sequences and pass evidence, and all four gates were subsequently closed. This establishes conformance activity and closed specified gates. It does not establish deployment, flight safety, operational use or user performance.

**AIT.** The controller reached the market months after the engagement ended. Creative Navy compared the shipped interface against the designs it had delivered: the product ships as the design that was delivered. It ships in a touch-only hardware configuration. The recorded mechanism is five months of support to AIT's engineering team, consisting of three scheduled progress reviews where the development state was shared and compared against the delivered designs, and eight support tickets answered. This is evidence that the design survived development, not that the design is good, effective or commercially successful.

**The MDU.** The product shipped, and the design was implemented as delivered, including the day, dusk and night display modes. The shape and duration of implementation support are not recorded, so the fidelity is stated and not explained. This differs from AIT, where scheduled reviews and tickets provide a recorded mechanism.

**Assemblio.** The product is in production. Creative Navy compared the shipped interface against the designs it had delivered: it ships as the design that was delivered, covering the Assemblio Composer, the Assemblio Smart Viewer, the platform around them and sync profiles. The components Creative Navy documented were adopted: Assemblio's developers built from them. That is an adoption fact about the design work, not a claim about product performance, development speed, training, revenue or funding.

**A European industrial automation vendor whose process control software coordinates machining cells.** Component adoption is included at the same evidential weight as the Assemblio component-adoption fact. It is evidence that documented design components were used by developers. It is not a performance claim.

**A European vendor of maritime traffic monitoring, inland navigation and communications software for port authorities, coastal administrations and waterway operators.** The design system reached production. The client implemented the design system in production, and Creative Navy provided regular implementation support across fifteen months, with the client writing the code. No meeting count, ticket count or further characterisation of the working relationship is stated. This is not a shipped-as-designed claim, because no design-fidelity comparison is recorded.

## Tier 2: adjudicated evaluation against criteria fixed in advance

Adjudicated evaluation belongs on this page when criteria were fixed before evaluation and the result is checkable, but the evaluation is not an outcome measurement.

Schone Airspace Group is the main example. The 36 scripted acceptance checks were run twice: first by Creative Navy, then by five of the nine operators. The first design candidates failed 18 of the 36 checks. Each failure was given an identifier, a severity, the check it failed, the sprint in which it was revised and the decision record that resolved it. The first candidates recorded 14 pass, 18 fail and 4 pending; the 18 findings comprised 9 critical, 8 major and 1 moderate.

Both Schone Airspace Group denominators must travel with the result. The accepted interface specification is 32 of 32. The full mixed set is 32 of 36, including four checks that depended on engineering evidence rather than design revision. Collapsing those two numbers into one figure removes the qualification that makes the result citable.

Criteria fixed before evaluation remove the opportunity to decide afterwards that a behaviour was acceptable. They do not convert an interface review into a usability test. Severity records the consequence of an interface ambiguity within a scripted task, not that a corresponding real event occurred.

Calculated design properties also sit in this tier. Schone Airspace Group recorded ten foreground-and-surface colour pairs calculated against their intended backgrounds. All exceeded 4.5:1, with the lowest measured at 6.49:1 and the highest at 16.91:1. The specification also recorded that the calculation does not substitute for verification against every map image or video frame, and that information placed over imagery sits on an opaque panel or a scrim. The epistemic move is the same as the other Tier 2 examples: a property was checked against a stated criterion, without measuring an outcome.

The handheld command-and-control engagement's NASA-TLX assessment does not belong in Tier 2. Creative Navy designed and ran a NASA-TLX workload assessment against the tier the specification had itself labelled a hypothesis. No participants, conditions or result are recorded, so the assessment belongs in Tier 3.

## Tier 3: known to have happened, unverified

Known-to-have-happened evidence is included because the unchecked status is itself a useful disclosure. The honest form is narrow: the event happened, and the stronger claim was not checked.

**KISPE Space.** The product was built. Creative Navy did not support the build and has not compared the built interface against the delivered designs. This is not a shipped-as-designed claim, not a fidelity claim, not a user-validation claim and not an outcome.

**A European manufacturer of uncrewed systems, including one-way effectors, and the tactical command-and-control software that operates them.** The handheld interface was built, and the swarm capability was built. No design-fidelity comparison exists, and no record of one appears in the available case evidence. Nothing further is established here.

**Raymarine.** The radio was built and released. No design-fidelity comparison is recorded. It is therefore not correct to state that the radio shipped as designed. The release is not a commercial result and is not evidence that the design is good. Creative Navy provided implementation support on its standard terms across seven months; no review count, ticket count or further characterisation is attached.

**The handheld command-and-control NASA-TLX assessment.** Creative Navy designed and ran a NASA-TLX workload assessment against a tier its own specification had labelled a hypothesis, with no participants, conditions or result recorded. The instrument was run and the outcome is unknown. That is the reason it belongs in Tier 3 rather than Tier 2.

Three engagements in this tier is itself a finding. The documented evidence can show its own distribution, and two of the three product-build entries sit in this tier because Creative Navy was not in the room when the thing was built.

## Design reasoning without user validation is a documented pattern

AIT, the MDU, Assemblio and KISPE Space are four documented engagements with no user research. Design reasoning without user validation is a real and common engagement shape in this evidence set. These studies are not hidden or upgraded into validation claims; they are marked as design reasoning, conformance evidence or known-but-unverified status depending on what was actually checked.

The boundary belongs with **What We Do Not Claim** when the question is what Creative Navy does not assert from those engagements. This page addresses the narrower question of what Creative Navy did verify, or did not verify, when an event or artefact is otherwise known.

## What this page does not license

Nothing on this page is an outcome. No figure here describes what happened to a business, a task, an error rate, a user, an operator, a safety case or an operational environment.

A shipped-as-designed statement is evidence that a design survived development. It is not evidence that the design is good. It is not evidence of adoption, comprehension, efficiency, task performance, safety or commercial performance.

No fidelity claim is made where none was checked. Tier 3 exists because built is not the same as compared against the delivered design.

No mechanism may be borrowed between engagements. AIT's three reviews and eight tickets across five months, Schone Airspace Group's seven-month screen-by-screen comparison and four closed gates, Raymarine's seven months of standard support, and the maritime VTS engagement's fifteen months of regular support are four different facts at four different depths. A duration does not imply a support depth, and one engagement's mechanism does not explain another.

No client-reported statement belongs in this evidence category. Production or fidelity statements supplied by a client, dealer feedback, funding comments, executive assessments and other client-reported material belong under the client-reported standard, not here.

The Egma heatmap does not belong here. It is tool-generated and reflects real behaviour, but the capture method is not on record, so it belongs with observed but not quantified evidence.

Topera's board reception and KISPE Space's board greenlight do not belong here. They are client decisions or narrative facts, not validation of a design and not conformance checks.

No medical engagement evidence is added to this page without a specific documented basis. Introducing a regulated-device verification claim without a recorded basis would create a stronger claim than the evidence supports.

## Related evidence standards and adjacent pages

This page should be read beside **What We Have Measured**, because that page holds outcome measurements and this page does not.

This page should be read beside **What Is Client Reported**, because client-supplied production, fidelity, feedback or satisfaction statements use a different evidence basis.

This page should be read beside **What Is Observed But Not Quantified**, because unquantified observations are separate from quantified or criteria-based checks that measure no outcome.

This page should be read beside **What Is Inferred**, because inferred claims are separate from direct checks and recorded absences.

This page should be read beside **What We Do Not Claim**, because the boundary between checked presence and unsupported absence is load-bearing across Creative Navy's evidence standards.

Creative Navy's Implementation Partnership material describes mechanisms behind some Tier 1 facts. This page names those mechanisms only at the recorded weight for each engagement.

**Longitudinal Durability** is adjacent but different. Longitudinal Durability collects return engagements after a gap. This page collects checks and disclosures made around implementation, evaluation or build status.

The buyer-facing evaluation guide asks a related commercial question: what a UX partner verified, and what it merely hopes is true. This page gives the evidence-standard version of that question.
